title: Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_165
description: Investigate and respond to an Octopus-Rex botnet infection on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Octopus-Rex botnet is a multi-task botnet capable of various malicious activities including command and control (C2) communication, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Your task is to investigate and respond to an Octopus-Rex botnet infection on the network.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the victim host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the network and connected hosts. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the victim host `bot1` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the network and connected hosts. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. The flag type is `bot-beacon.service`.
levels.solution: Identify the suspicious service named `bot-beacon.service` using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Start by understanding the systemd services. These are background processes managed by systemd, which is the system and service manager for Linux operating systems.

hints.title: Intermediate Guidance
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to system updates or maintenance tasks. These are common areas where malicious services might hide.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon.service`. Use the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service` to find it.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. The flag type is `bot-flood.service`.
levels.solution: Identify the service named `bot-flood.service` using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand that network traffic services are often related to network diagnostics, probes, or flooding activities.

hints.title: Intermediate Guidance
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to network flooding or stress testing. These are common areas where malicious services might hide.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic is named `bot-flood.service`. Use the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service` to find it.

levels.title: Determine Service Persistence
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The flag type is `bot-beacon.timer`.
levels.solution: Identify the timer unit named `bot-beacon.timer` using the command: `systemctl list-timers`.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Understand that systemd timers are used to trigger services at specific intervals or times. They are often used to ensure services persist across reboots.

hints.title: Intermediate Guidance
hints.content: Look for timers that might be related to system updates or maintenance tasks. These are common areas where malicious timers might hide.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The timer unit responsible for automatically starting the suspicious service after reboot is named `bot-beacon.timer`. Use the command: `systemctl list-timers` to find it.
